title: Holeshot HUD — What's new
question: After an in-app update, Settings shows this version's notes. Pick the composition. What should carry forward? What feels false to Broadcast Booth Glass?

options.label: Center Plaque
options.thesis: A centered charcoal board with an orange version plaque owns the window; Settings waits behind a dim scrim until they hit Got it.
options.viewport: Dimmed Settings chrome (Widgets / Settings / Feedback) fills the 1000×720 window. Center: a ~520px charcoal panel, 10px corners. Orange skew plaque is the heading — 0.1.17 — not an eyebrow. Headline under it, then OVERLAY / SETTINGS uppercase labels and bullets. Full-width orange Got it along the bottom edge of the panel.
options.risk: A centered dialog can read as generic app chrome if the plaque is a rounded card instead of a TV skew bar.

options.label: Lower Third
options.thesis: Notes arrive as a TV lower-third across the bottom of Settings — the pit wall still visible above, the board the only new hardware.
options.viewport: Settings remains fully composed in the top 55%. A wide night-ink board spans the bottom: orange skew left end holds 0.1.17, headline runs the bar, bullets sit in one tight column, orange Got it is a plaque on the right end of the bar.
options.risk: A thin bar will clip the bullets; if it grows too tall it stops being a lower-third and becomes a second window.

options.label: Pane Board
options.thesis: The notes replace the Settings pane the way a widget tab does: same Show plaque chrome, Got it where Show on overlay sits.
options.viewport: Top mode bar and left widget rail stay. The content pane opens on a full-width orange name plaque: 0.1.17 on the left, Got it on the right. Headline and changelog bullets stack below as standings-like rows with OVERLAY / SETTINGS group labels.
options.risk: Without a scrim it can feel like another Settings tab instead of an update they must acknowledge.
